summary: Normal systems remain broadly functional, but multiple leading indicators are deteriorating. Complete reasonable preparations before shortages or access constraints worsen.
primary_driver: Energy security and Gulf shipping disruption are the strongest near-term pathways to wider civilian-facing economic stress.
primary_stabilizers: Global trade, finance, and energy systems are still functioning and adapting.
No direct NATO–Russia or U.S.–China war is underway.
Alternative energy routes, reserves, and diplomatic channels continue to provide partial buffers.

domains.name: Energy security
domains.rationale: Oil prices are above $100 and Hormuz traffic remains sharply reduced, though alternative routes and supply adaptation are limiting broader failure.

domains.name: Military / geopolitical
domains.rationale: The U.S.–Iran conflict and continuing Russia–Ukraine spillover risks elevate escalation pressure without yet producing direct great-power war.

domains.name: Supply chain & transportation
domains.rationale: Shipping risk, rerouting, insurance costs, and energy-related freight pressure are affecting global logistics.

domains.name: Global trade fragmentation
domains.rationale: U.S.–Canada retaliation and wider tariff/export-control frictions are increasing costs and strategic supply-chain fragmentation.

domains.name: Technology chokepoints
domains.rationale: Rare-earth and strategic-material access remains vulnerable to geopolitical restrictions and supplier hesitation.

domains.name: Critical infrastructure / cyber
domains.rationale: Subsea infrastructure and energy-sector cyber threats are elevated, but widespread civilian outages are not occurring.

domains.name: Financial-system stress
domains.rationale: High energy prices, inflation pressure, and elevated bond yields are stressing markets, while the IMF still reports broad global resilience.

domains.name: Food & agriculture
domains.rationale: Energy, fertilizer, freight, and tariff costs are lifting input pressures, but a global food-supply emergency is not present.

domains.name: Domestic institutional stress
domains.rationale: Political and policy friction is elevated in several countries without broad loss of institutional capacity.

domains.name: Public health / biological
domains.rationale: No current public-health event is producing globally systemic disruption.

domains.name: Natural / environmental
domains.rationale: No current natural event is producing globally systemic disruption.

areas_to_watch.name: Hormuz shipping & oil flows
areas_to_watch.why: Further tanker attacks or a deeper traffic collapse could rapidly transmit into fuel, freight, inflation, and industrial costs.

areas_to_watch.name: U.S.–Canada / global tariff escalation
areas_to_watch.why: Further retaliation or expansion into strategic sectors could deepen cross-border cost and availability pressure.

areas_to_watch.name: Strategic cyber threats
areas_to_watch.why: Energy, telecom, financial, and subsea infrastructure remain high-consequence targets with little civilian warning time.

areas_to_watch.name: Financial stress / credit markets
areas_to_watch.why: Energy-driven inflation and high yields could become more disruptive if liquidity or credit conditions deteriorate materially.

areas_to_watch.name: Export controls & rare earths
areas_to_watch.why: Restrictions on critical minerals and industrial inputs can create delayed but significant technology and manufacturing bottlenecks.

signals.title: Hormuz shipping traffic falls to single digits
signals.summary: Vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz dropped to seven on Wednesday, while alternative Saudi Red Sea export routes are carrying more volume.

signals.title: Oil surges above $100 on renewed tanker attacks
signals.summary: Brent and U.S. crude both rose above $100 as attacks on shipping and energy infrastructure increased supply-risk premiums.

signals.title: Canada's new counter-tariffs take effect
signals.summary: Canada imposed 15%, 25%, and 50% counter-tariffs on C$27.6 billion of U.S. products across steel, dairy, appliances, farm equipment, paper, plastics, and electronics.

signals.title: U.S. broadens retaliation against Canadian imports
signals.summary: The U.S. Trade Representative announced targeted import bans and tariff adjustments in response to Canada's retaliatory measures.

signals.title: NATO allies disrupted suspected subsea cable sabotage training
signals.summary: Reuters reported that allied forces confronted a Russian undersea operation involving technology designed to disable critical subsea cables.

signals.title: IMF says global growth remains resilient despite energy shock
signals.summary: The IMF still expects roughly 3% global growth in 2026 while warning that energy prices, debt pressure, and uncertainty remain high.

signals.title: Some Chinese rare-earth suppliers halt U.S. shipments
signals.summary: Supplier reluctance and export-license friction are keeping several critical materials tight ahead of high-level U.S.–China meetings.

preparedness_actions: Maintain several weeks of normal food and household consumables.
Keep prescriptions and essential medical supplies current.
Maintain a reasonable amount of emergency cash alongside normal banking access.
Verify generator, battery, solar, or other backup-power capability.
Confirm family communications and meeting plans.
historical_note: Illustrative reference markers only; not used in the live score until formal back-testing is completed.

methodology.note: All-hazards early-warning assessment, not a probability forecast or prediction that a specific disaster will occur.
methodology.formula: Leading Threat Pressure = mean of the four highest domain threat scores. Observed Civilian Disruption = mean of the four highest domain impact scores. Preparedness Urgency = 55% Leading Threat Pressure + 30% Observed Civilian Disruption + 15% Cross-System Coupling, rounded.
methodology.stage_guardrails: IMMINENT DISRUPTION requires both a high urgency score and material observed disruption. ACTIVE DISRUPTION requires broad, documented system impairment; threat scores alone cannot trigger it.
methodology.domains: Military/geopolitical, energy, trade, supply chain, technology, critical infrastructure/cyber, financial, food/agriculture, domestic institutional, public health, and natural/environmental.
